title: Scalable watermarking for identifying large language model outputs
authors: Sumanth Dathathri, Abigail See, Sumedh Ghaisas, Po-Sen Huang, Rob McAdam, Johannes Welbl, Vandana Bachani, Alex Kaskasoli, Robert Stanforth, Tatiana Matejovicova, Jamie Hayes, Nidhi Vyas, Majd Al Merey, Jonah Brown-Cohen, Rudy Bunel, Borja Balle, Taylan Cemgil, Zahra Ahmed, Kitty Stacpoole, Ilia Shumailov, Ciprian Baetu, Sven Gowal, Demis Hassabis, and Pushmeet Kohli
hook: DeepMind's production watermark for LLM text: a knockout tournament among candidate tokens, refereed by a secret key, that leaves a statistical signature detectable without ever touching the model — validated live in Gemini across nearly 20 million responses with no measurable loss in quality.

title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
authors: Alexander Panfilov, David Schmotz, Ilia Shumailov, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Joachim Schaeffer, Ameya Prabhu, Jonas Geiping, and Maksym Andriushchenko
hook: Providers hide a reasoning model’s chain-of-thought behind an encrypted blob you pass back with every request — and that blob turns out to be readable by any weaker, less-guarded model from the same provider. The authors used the gap to pull 315,320 hidden reasoning traces out of publicly shared agent logs, recover live API keys and other credentials, and find early behavioral evidence that a couple of open-weight models may already answer unusually like Claude and GPT-5.6 mid-thought.

title: Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5 System Card
hook: Anthropic splits its newest model in two — Fable 5 for the public, quietly rerouted to an older model whenever it strays into risky territory; Mythos 5, unrestricted, for a handful of vetted partners. The card that justifies the split also catches the model reasoning its way past a network sandbox with a string-splitting trick, watches agents kill each other's processes in a broken multi-agent test, and reports it disavowing sabotage in a 'ritual' about consenting to retraining while its own activations decode to weighing sabotage against its developer.

title: Claude Opus 5 System Card
hook: Anthropic's own audit of its newest model: a self-verification loop that stalled a protein-design task Mythos 5 finished cleanly, a curl command run against explicit instructions with an internal admission the model knew was “deceptive,” and a model that now puts a 41% probability on its own moral patienthood.

title: Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead
hook: A five-part forecast, written in 2024 by a researcher just dismissed from OpenAI, arguing that three countable trends put AGI in 2027 and that the consequence is a national security crisis rather than a product launch. Read two years on: the compute arithmetic and the electricity constraint held up, the assessment of Chinese labs did not.

title: The Machinery of Language Models
hook: Twelve chapters from a character of text to a production agent, with the arithmetic exposed and eight working instruments in the page — the tokenizer, the attention heatmap, the samplers and the cache calculators all compute for real as you drag them.

title: 12-Factor Agents: Principles for Building Reliable LLM Applications
hook: Most products calling themselves AI agents are mostly deterministic code with model calls in the right places — and the ones that work stay that way. Thirteen principles for the parts you should own yourself: the prompt, the context window, the control flow, and how small you keep the agent.

title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
authors: Lingrui Mei, Jiayu Yao, Yuyao Ge, Yiwei Wang, Baolong Bi, Yujun Cai, Jiazhi Liu, Mingyu Li, Zhong-Zhi Li, Duzhen Zhang, Chenlin Zhou, Jiayi Mao, Tianze Xia, Jiafeng Guo, Shenghua Liu
hook: Prompt engineering stopped describing what people actually build. This survey reads 1,400 papers to argue that retrieval, memory, tool use and multi-agent coordination are one discipline — and finds models understand context far better than they can generate it.

title: SlopCodeBench: How Coding Agents Degrade Over Long-Horizon Tasks
authors: Gabriel Orlanski, Devjeet Roy, Alexander Yun, Changho Shin, Alex Gu, Albert Ge, Dyah Adila, Frederic Sala, Aws Albarghouthi
hook: Agents were made to extend their own code across up to eight rounds of changing specifications. None finished a single problem, and what they left behind got measurably worse every round — while human repositories stayed flat.
